title: How long have you been working on your current game, or when did you start working on it?

posts.author: SuperPhillip
posts.body:
Hi, all! The idea for this topic--and here's hoping I didn't miss an already-made topic full of fun discussion--came from realizing that I've spent over a decade (this will be my 11th year) doing off and on (mostly off) work on my RPG Maker game. There have been so many changes, enhancements, and upgrades, as I continue to build the scenario for the game. It's a bit overwhelming and exhausting to look back at and say, "Omigosh, I have done a LOT of work and there's still a fair amount more to do!" That said, it's been
mostly
fun all the way. Oh, and just for a quick reminder that isn't at all inspired by my previous statement--always have multiple backups of your project is a good rule to have. Just saying for no real reason. ^_^;
But yeah, how long have you been working on your game? Or better yet, how long has it been since you've started your current project, as not everyone probably goes all in with development all the time due to other obligations and such!

posts.author: firestalker
posts.body:
My current game has been in the works for 5 or more years... off and on, mostly off. I started it as a way to test out different puzzle ideas in a game setting, and it quickly evolved into my main game since I was having fun with it.
Now I'm working on it pretty steady at the moment, so I was finally able to release a portion of it for playtesting [My difficulty balance needs work]...

posts.author: Lucidia
posts.body: Started my current project back in Oct 2021, just over 4 years so far. Definitely a labor of love!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
fwiw, the ideal turn around on an indie project (or really, any game project but AAA won't listen) is about 3 years.
How many actually are able to achieve that? Probably very few. It's too easy to overscope, plan poorly, and let the project run amok.
I can sit here and preach "about 3 years" all I want, but my project was started in 2022, and I'd estimate 2 more years of development.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: The one I'm currently polishing off was started before I even bought RPGMaker (using the trial version), which would be a bit before I created an account here. However, it spent most of that time sitting in limbo. I think I've only done about 2 years worth of work on it, one of which was the past year of continuous work.

posts.author: LowrellLovelace
posts.body: Around the start of last November. But I spent most of it trying to learn to code. I've made maps with all the default assets but I only plan to use them as placeholders. It's probably going to be a while to make anything decent since I've only actively practicing drawing and music for half a week. I also chronically upload my work to a separate hard drive incase my computer keels over.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
I think that I started my "current" project in July 2025. Fairly soon after I got MZ I decided to convert what I had  to MZ. However, since then I have side-tracked, converting a previously finished project to MZ, upgrading some of the gameplay and mechanics. I hope to get back to my paused "current" project within a month or two.
My last completed game took from January 2024 to July 2025. I really ought to be looking for ways to put it on the Internet as a freebie.
My first attempt started fairly soon after I got VX, when VX was the latest version of RPG Maker. Partially completed versions have been converted to VX Ace and to MV, changing substantially and losing content during each conversion. I have a feeling that it isn't going to be finished anytime soon.

posts.author: Indinera
posts.body: My current game is a collaboration with another dev so currently only one month more or less, but I generally need 3-6 months to complete and release a full game, sometimes less especially in my prime lol

posts.author: mirrormagic
posts.body:
I first thought about my main game in August last year, but I spent a lot of that time procrastinating so this year, I'm just aiming to get the first 3 out of 10 or so days in the story done!
I think I've improved a lot since I first started XD

posts.author: ArtoriasDeathh
posts.body:
I actually started about two weeks ago, this is my first real project.
I jumped in with a pretty ambitious scope right away, which in hindsight might have been a bit much considering I didn’t have prior experience or advanced skills in art or storytelling. That said, I’ve been learning quickly and improving as I go.
I’ve already clocked nearly 170 hours in a short time, which honestly forced me to take a break to avoid burning out and play some video games.
I do use AI for enemy graphics since I’m not an artist and don’t currently have the budget to commission or purchase large asset packs. Even so, creating enemies that properly fit the game’s lore and aesthetic still takes a significant amount of time. Getting one enemy to feel “right” is rarely quick.
Given the current scope multiple endings, branching choices, large map regions, cities, and side quests I expect Act 1 alone to take around three months if development stays consistent. The full game will likely take years to complete.
I’ve also been considering releasing the game act by act rather than waiting for the full version to be finished.

posts.author: Juanita
posts.body:
I think before 2016 or 2017. I was expecting working for a year or so. The game continued to grow bigger than I expected.  Waiting for spritework was a big problem. It was a very long wait that kinda killed the rythm. Also, the need for it to be perfect. That was a personal problem.
I took a break then came back this year with a new perspective.  No need to be perfect, it just need to be.

posts.author: lianderson
posts.body: 14 years.

posts.author: OmlyUltra
posts.body: I started my first (and only) RPG Maker project on the 3rd of Jan this year. I've been putting about 2-4 hours of work into it a day, and a lot of it is breaking and fixing things as I try to learn RPG Maker MZ at the same time. The project originally started off as a combat prototype, but it's been really fun to expand it! I have no idea when it'll be done, I try not to get bit by scope creep, but I'm just a guy. Hopefully my first major area of the game post-tutorial will be done by the end of March, and we'll play it by ear onwards (there's 4 major areas + some extra stuff I've planned).

posts.author: Plueschkatze
posts.body: For The Herzbury Curse... I did work on it in 2018/2019 for a few months, but had to put the project on ice, because life happens, and started new in Dezember 25, released a demo start of february and hope to release the full game still in 26.

posts.author: ArtistocrArt
posts.body: I joined a game development in the summer of 2024 as the sole artist, and almost 2 years later we're still working hard to get to release. We haven't worked on it since last November though, because my dev friend needed help with another project he was working on prior to ours, so we pressed pause on our game to finish up his project first.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
I don't really have a single "current game". I've shifted toward making multiple short prototypes for more casual lightweight games and moved to another engine for it. I've also lately been making concept art rather than working with code.
I'd like to experiment with different concepts and gauge player reaction before going all in one project.

posts.author: SuperPhillip
posts.body:
Decidedly and understandably a lot of different starts and duration for game projects. Yeah, a major factor for sure in making an RPG on the side is that it sometimes does take a backseat to life. For me, it can be a mix of that and just having a different hyperfocus with my autism. When I get really engaged with my game, I get REALLY engaged, but I also sometimes periodically burn out and run on fumes for a while, too. Not the most optimal way of making a game. ha
All the same, I hope you're all having a lot of fun with your individual and respective projects, and that you're able to get a good deal of work done too! The bonus, of course, is if you finish said project, which is always a rewarding feeling. But, even making steps towards finishing a project is rewarding all to itself, whether identifying and solving a problem that pops up or finishing a map after days of starting on it.
